title: GrantDesk: multi-client workspace for freelance grant writers
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: One workspace for freelance grant writers to manage all their clients: deadlines, reusable text per client, report reminders and AI first drafts. Existing tools are built for one organisation, not a consultant with many clients.
hook: "I have twelve clients, forty deadlines and my boilerplate is spread across a hundred Word files."
story:
**Rachel is a freelance grant writer with 12 nonprofit clients.** Each client has its own mission text, budgets, past applications and funder reports due on different dates. She tracks deadlines in a spreadsheet and keeps text in **folders full of Word files**.

Twice last year she nearly missed a **funder report deadline** because it was buried in an email. Tools like Instrumentl are great for finding funders but are built for one organisation, not a consultant juggling many. Rachel wants one place with client folders, a text library per client, a deadline calendar and a status link she can send to each client.
whyNow: Grant software is a proven paid category: Instrumentl starts at $179/month and Grantable at $50/month, and Grantable claims 30,000+ grant professionals as users. AI now writes good first drafts from a client's own past text. There is no regulatory deadline.
evidence: Instrumentl plans start at $179/month; Grantable paid plans start at $50/month (pricing as of May 2026) [Grantable]
Grantable claims 30,000+ grant professionals as users (vendor claim) [Grantable]
A third-party review lists Grantable at free / $50 / $150 per month (unverified) [aitoolsbakery]
Many small new entrants on Capterra, e.g. Imagagrant and ScriptaGrant [Capterra]
Pain evidence is indirect: no survey of grant-writer hours or missed deadlines was found [Top 25 report]

whyReal.title: People already pay for grant tools
whyReal.text: Instrumentl ($179+) and Grantable ($50–150) show grant professionals pay monthly for software.

whyReal.title: Consultants juggle many clients
whyReal.text: A freelancer with 5–20 clients has many deadlines and many text libraries. Tools built for one nonprofit do not fit.

whyReal.title: Missed deadlines cost money
whyReal.text: A missed application or late report can lose a grant and a client. (To confirm in interviews: no survey was found.)

whyReal.title: Easy-to-find buyers
whyReal.text: Grant writers list themselves on LinkedIn, Upwork and Fiverr, so Jonatan can build a lead list quickly.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Freelance grant writers and consultants managing 5–20 clients, and small nonprofits with budgets under $2M.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The consultant, or the nonprofit's director.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: English-speaking freelance grant writers (US, UK, Canada, Australia), found on LinkedIn and Upwork.

solution.title: Pipeline board
solution.text: each application moves through prospect, drafting, submitted, awarded and reporting.

solution.title: Deadline reminders
solution.text: email reminders for application and report deadlines across all clients.

solution.title: Library per client
solution.text: documents and boilerplate stored per client, searchable with AI.

solution.title: AI first drafts
solution.text: draft sections from the client's library and the pasted funder guidelines.

solution.title: Client status link
solution.text: a shareable page so each client sees progress without emails.

must: Grant pipeline board (prospect, drafting, submitted, awarded, reporting)
Email reminders for deadlines and reports
Document and boilerplate library per client with AI search
AI drafts of sections from the library and pasted funder guidelines
later: Export drafts to Word with formatting
Time tracking and invoicing for consultants

techStack: LLM for drafting (RAG over client library)

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Message 150 freelance grant writers on LinkedIn and Upwork; hold 10 interviews; show a clickable prototype (Figma or similar). Target: 5 consultants agree to a $99 founding-member pre-sale or paid pilot.
Victor builds client workspaces, pipeline board and deadline reminders.
Library with AI search, AI drafts, client status link, Stripe.
Onboard founding members and iterate on their feedback.

costs.note: Vercel + Supabase free or low tiers
Resend / Postmark free or low tiers
No-code builder or built by us

costTotal3Months: ≈ €450–700 (report estimate €150–250 for hosting, AI and validation, plus €300–450 for AI coding tools)

competitors.name: Instrumentl
competitors.gap: Strong on finding funders; not built for multi-client consultants

competitors.name: Us
competitors.what: Client folders, text library per client, deadline calendar, client status page
competitors.gap: Built for the consultant with many clients

risks.answer: Sell the multi-client workspace and deadlines, not the AI writing.
Target consultants first: they bill clients and feel the pain directly.
Do not build a funder database; users bring their own funders.

questions: How many clients and applications do you juggle per month?
How do you track deadlines and reporting duties today?
Where does your reusable text live, and how do you adapt it?
Which tools do you pay for now, and what do you dislike about them?
What has a missed deadline or late report cost you?

numbers.competition: Crowded AI writers; consultant niche open
